The issue changes prose only: the pages that tell whoever edits this repository how to write a rule, and the frontmatter descriptions those rules are then applied to.

The authoring rules are split across two pages, and neither is a general one; which of them houses the new material — or whether a rule that binds both belongs in a single home the other points at — is the first thing the increment has to settle from the pages themselves:

- `skills/CLAUDE.md` — the authoring rules for skill pages: what a page has to carry (frontmatter `name`/`description`/`user-invocable`, the body), "Interface and inside", "Where a rule belongs", "Assets". Its "What a page has to carry" already states what a skill `description` is for, so the description rule lands on or against that text.
- `.claude/rules/agents.md` — the authoring rules for agent pages, path-scoped to `agents/**`: what an agent page has to carry (frontmatter `name`/`description`/`tools`/`skills`/`color`, the body), "The page is the interface", and the rules about where a rule that binds agents may live. Its "What a page has to carry" states what an agent `description` is for.

The descriptions the new rule is applied to:

- `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md` — shipped skill; its `description` is checked against the description rule and rewritten if it summarises steps. It is also the one home for a rule that binds every agent, so it is in scope if the description rule turns out to bind agents at run time rather than only their authors.
- `skills/argus/SKILL.md` — shipped skill description, checked and rewritten if it summarises steps.
- `skills/grill/SKILL.md` — shipped skill description, checked and rewritten if it summarises steps.
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` — shipped skill description, checked and rewritten if it summarises steps.
- `agents/planner.md` — agent description, checked against the rule and rewritten only where it contradicts the body of its own page.
- `agents/researcher.md` — same.
- `agents/implementer.md` — same.
- `agents/reviewer.md` — same.
- `agents/test-author.md` — same.

One file may be touched depending on how the change is verified:

- `test-repo.sh` — the suite that owns facts about the repository itself (licence claims, `paths:` frontmatter on `.claude/rules/*.md`) and the only existing home for a mechanical check over these pages; it is listed in `test.sh` and needs no new entry there.

Checked and out of scope: `rulebook.md` and `GEMINI.md` steer the session's own conduct and carry no rules about writing a page's frontmatter or a rule's form; `README.md` paraphrases the skills but copies no frontmatter description verbatim; the suite docs under `hooks/`, `tools/*/` and `skills/agent-brief/assets/` document test suites, not authoring.

increments.title: The authoring rules pick a rule's form by the failure it prevents
increments.goal: Whoever edits a page in this repository finds in the authoring rules a four-row table that picks the form of a correction from the failure class it prevents, and a standing ban on patching a working rule with an exemption clause. Today that choice is made by taste and re-learned through failed agent runs.
criteria: The authoring rules carry a table of exactly four rows; each row names a failure class, the form that works against it, the form that fails against it, and the reason in one sentence.

The four rows are: a rule skipped under pressure gets a prohibition carrying its price and the verbatim rationalisation it counters; a wrong output shape gets a recipe stating what the output is; an omitted required element gets a required slot in the schema or template; behaviour that depends on a condition gets a rule keyed to an observable predicate.
The authoring rules forbid patching an existing rule with an exemption clause and require re-cutting the rule on an observable predicate instead.

The table and the exemption rule reach whoever authors a skill page and whoever authors an agent page alike, and the repository's existing rule about one home per rule is not broken to achieve it — no page restates what another page already carries.
The commands the increment names all exit 0.

return.plan:
SCOPE. Increment 1 is the four-row form table and the ban on exemption clauses, reaching whoever authors a skill page and whoever authors an agent page alike. The description rule and the sweep of shipped descriptions belong to a later increment: touch no frontmatter `description` anywhere, and change no agent page and no shipped SKILL.md.

DECISION 1 — THE HOME. Create a new page `.claude/rules/authoring.md`, path-scoped to both audiences:

---
paths:
  - "skills/**"
  - "agents/**"
---

Why there. The rule binds whoever *writes* a page in this checkout, not an agent at run time. `.claude/rules/agents.md` (lines 58-63) states the test: a page under `.claude/rules/` may only carry what someone developing uroboros needs, and may never be the only home of a rule that binds a run. An authoring rule for uroboros's own prose pages is exactly the first and not the second. The same page (lines 15-20) records the measured mechanic this relies on: a path-scoped rule is not inherited at launch, but a reader that opens a matching file loads it for itself, subagents included. So one page reaches both authoring audiences with no restatement anywhere and no hop. Confirmed against the Claude Code memory docs ('Path-specific rules'): `paths` takes a YAML list of glob patterns, and path-scoped rules trigger when a matching file is read. Confirmed against `test-repo.sh` lines 99-105: its `scope.js` parser already reads the list form, so the two existing cases in the '=== no repository-local rule reaches an agent' section (every rules page is scoped; every pattern matches tracked files) guard the new page for free, with no change to them.

Rejected alternatives.
(a) `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md`, the shared brief. `skills/CLAUDE.md`'s 'Where a rule belongs' sends a rule that binds more than one skill or agent to the brief, but that section is about rules that bind agents *at run time* — its own justification is 'Nothing else reaches every agent'. The brief ships with the plugin and is injected into every agent on every run in every project; the planner, reviewer, test-author and researcher never author a uroboros page, and no installing project has uroboros pages to author. `.claude/rules/agents.md` lines 46-47 draw the same line: 'This page is for whoever writes the agents; the shared brief is for the agents.'
(b) The table in `skills/CLAUDE.md`, with a pointer from `.claude/rules/agents.md`. Rejected: that page is titled 'The skills' and loads only for a reader working under `skills/`, so an agent-page author reaches the rule only through a hop that costs a read and can be skipped. Criterion 4 asks that it reach both alike.
(c) One rules page scoped `**/*.md`. Rejected: it matches `docs/issues/**`, so every agent that reads its issue file would load the authoring rules it has no use for.

DECISION 2 — WHAT THE NEW PAGE SAYS. Keep it short (roughly 30-40 lines) and in this order:

1. Title `# The form of a rule`.
2. One framing sentence: the rows below come from measured head-to-head wording tests (obra/superpowers, `skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md`, 'Match the Form to the Failure'), so a row changes on a measurement and not on taste.
3. One markdown table — the only table on the page — with the header `Failure class | Form that works | Form that fails | Why` and exactly four body rows:
   - A rule skipped under pressure | A prohibition that carries its price and quotes, verbatim, the rationalisation it counters | An unpriced reminder to keep the rule in mind | Under pressure an agent trades away a rule whose cost of skipping is unnamed, and an unquoted excuse stays available.
   - A wrong output shape | A recipe that states what the output is | A list of prohibitions | A ban names what not to emit and leaves the shape unstated, which measured worse than no guidance at all.
   - An omitted required element | A required slot in the schema or the template | Prose in the body asking for the element | A slot makes the omission visible in the artefact, while prose is satisfied by an agent that believes it complied.
   - Behaviour that depends on a condition | A rule keyed to an observable predicate | A judgement call, or an exemption bolted onto the general rule | A predicate the agent can evaluate decides both branches, and a judgement call decides neither.
4. The ban, as its own short paragraph below the table, in the imperative: never patch a working rule with an exemption clause; re-cut the rule on an observable predicate instead, stating the two branches separately — one appended exemption measured a working rule down from consistent to noisy.
5. One closing sentence saying why the page is repo-local: it binds whoever writes a page here rather than an agent at run time, so it stays out of the shipped brief.

HARD CONSTRAINTS the suite keys on — honour these exactly or the checks fail:
- Exactly one markdown table on the page: a header row, a separator row, and four body rows, each on one line, each with exactly four non-empty cells.
- The fourth cell of every body row is one sentence: it ends with a single full stop and contains no other full stop, so no abbreviation such as 'e.g.' inside it.
- Row 1's line carries the words 'skipped under pressure', 'prohibition', 'price' and 'rationalisation'. British spelling throughout, as the repository uses elsewhere ('behaviour', 'licence'): 'rationalisation', never 'rationalization'.
- Row 2's line carries 'shape' and 'recipe'.
- Row 3's line carries 'omitted', 'slot', and 'schema' or 'template'.
- Row 4's line carries 'condition' and 'observable predicate'.
- The exact phrase 'exemption clause' appears in the ban paragraph and nowhere else in the repository outside `docs/issues/`. That is why row 4's failing form is worded 'an exemption bolted onto the general rule' rather than with the phrase, and why neither pointer below may use it.
- The ban paragraph also carries 're-cut' and 'observable predicate'.
- The word 'rationalisation' likewise appears on this page alone outside `docs/issues/`.

DECISION 3 — THE TWO POINTERS. A pointer names the owner; it never summarises it. One sentence each, naming the path `.claude/rules/authoring.md` and none of the page's content:
- `skills/CLAUDE.md`, appended to the end of 'Where a rule belongs': say that this section decides where a rule lives, while `.claude/rules/authoring.md` decides what form it takes, and that the latter stays out of the brief because it binds whoever writes a page here rather than an agent at run time. That sentence also keeps 'Where a rule belongs' honest about the new page, so a reader cannot read the section as sending an authoring rule to the brief.
- `.claude/rules/agents.md`, one sentence after the paragraph ending 'A rule that stands in both drifts.' (line 73): the form a rule on an agent page takes is `.claude/rules/authoring.md`.

DECISION 4 — WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. No `plugin.json` entry: `.claude/rules/` is not shipped and is declared nowhere. No `README.md` change: it lists no rule pages. No `test.sh` change: `test-repo.sh` is already listed there. No agent page, no shipped `SKILL.md`, no frontmatter description.

return.testPlan:
TESTS ARE NEEDED. The change is prose, but every acceptance criterion of this increment is a mechanically checkable fact about files, and `test-repo.sh` is this repository's established home for exactly that.

WHERE THE CASES GO. All of them are bash cases appended to `/home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh` as one new section, placed after the '=== remote operation deploys the collector alone' section and before the final summary block (`if [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]`, lines 2211-2218). Framework: none — the file is plain bash with `set -u`, counting through the `ok` and `no` helpers defined at lines 11-12 and exiting 1 when any case failed. Follow the file's own conventions, visible in the '=== the mutation standard has one owner' section (lines 473-548): open with `echo` then `echo "=== <heading>"`, put a comment above each case naming the criterion it proves and the Break that makes it fail, and use `$root` for every path. Heading for the new section: `=== a rule's form is picked by the failure it prevents`.

SUITE DOC. There is no `CLAUDE.md` suite doc for `test-repo.sh`, and none may be created: the doc would have to sit at the repository root, and this same suite fails if a root `CLAUDE.md` exists ('no CLAUDE.md at the repository root', lines 176-180). The existing '=== every test suite carries its doc' case only covers directories holding a `*.test.mjs`, which this file is not. So write no suite doc for this suite; the file's own header comment and the section style above are its conventions.

LEVEL. Every case below is a repository-fact case in that one file, run by the one command in `environment`. No unit or end-to-end level applies — there is no code under test.

CASES.

Criterion 1 (a table of exactly four rows, each with a failure class, the form that works, the form that fails, and a one-sentence reason):

1. Four body rows, four non-empty cells each. Parse `.claude/rules/authoring.md` in an inline `node -e` block: collect the lines whose first non-space character is `|`, drop the first (the header) and the separator line (cells of dashes and colons only), and assert exactly four remain, each splitting into exactly four cells that are non-empty after trimming. Expected: pass. Break: add a fifth row, delete one, or blank the 'form that fails' cell of any row.
2. Each reason is one sentence. In the same parse, assert the fourth cell of every body row matches `/^[^.]+\.$/` — one full stop, at the end. Expected: pass. Break: split any reason cell into two sentences.

Criterion 2 (the four rows are the named four). One case per row, each asserting a single line of the file carries the failure class and its winning form together, so a row cannot be satisfied by words scattered over the page. Chain greps on the file, case-insensitively, e.g. `grep -i 'skipped under pressure' "$root/.claude/rules/authoring.md" | grep -i 'prohibition' | grep -i 'price' | grep -qi 'rationalisation'`:

3. Row 1: one line carries 'skipped under pressure', 'prohibition', 'price' and 'rationalisation'. Expected: pass. Break: drop the price, or the verbatim rationalisation, from row 1's winning form.
4. Row 2: one line carries 'shape' and 'recipe'. Expected: pass. Break: change row 2's winning form to a list of prohibitions.
5. Row 3: one line carries 'omitted', 'slot', and 'schema' or 'template'. Expected: pass. Break: replace the required slot with prose asking for the element.
6. Row 4: one line carries 'condition' and 'observable predicate'. Expected: pass. Break: re-key row 4 on a judgement call instead of a predicate.

Criterion 3 (the ban on exemption clauses, and the re-cut it requires):

7. The ban is on the page, both halves. Collapse the page to one line (`tr '\n' ' ' | tr -s ' '`, as the file already does at lines 533 and 553) and assert it carries 'exemption clause', 're-cut' and 'observable predicate'. Expected: pass. Break: delete the ban paragraph — 'exemption clause' and 're-cut' both vanish, since row 4's failing form is worded without either.

Criterion 4 (both authoring audiences are reached, and no page restates another):

8. The home page exists and is scoped to both audiences. Assert `.claude/rules/authoring.md` exists, and that its frontmatter `paths:` block lists both `skills/**` and `agents/**` (grep the lines between the two `---` fences). Expected: pass. Break: drop either pattern from the list, or delete the file — one of the two audiences stops loading the rule. Note for context: the suite's existing scoping cases (lines 68-123) additionally prove the new page is path-scoped at all and that both patterns match tracked files; they need no edit and are not restated here.
9. The skill-page author is pointed at the home. Assert `skills/CLAUDE.md` names `.claude/rules/authoring.md`. Expected: pass. Break: delete that pointer sentence.
10. The agent-page author is pointed at the home. Assert `.claude/rules/agents.md` names `.claude/rules/authoring.md`. Expected: pass. Break: delete that pointer sentence.
11. One home for the ban. Mirror the `chain_depth_owners` case (lines 455-461): `grep -lie 'exemption clause' "$root"/agents/*.md "$root"/skills/*/SKILL.md "$root/skills/CLAUDE.md" "$root"/.claude/rules/*.md "$root/rulebook.md" "$root/README.md" "$root/GEMINI.md"` must equal `$root/.claude/rules/authoring.md` exactly. Expected: pass. Break, either direction: restate the ban on a second page (two paths match), or delete it from the owner (none match).
12. One home for the table. The same ownership check over the same file set, keyed on 'rationalisation'. Expected: pass. Break, either direction: restate a table row on another page, or delete row 1 from the owner.

WHAT IS LEFT UNTESTED, AND WHY. The 'reason in one sentence' clause of criterion 1 is checked structurally (case 2) rather than semantically — that the cell is one sentence, not that the sentence is a reason; judging a reason is a reading, and the reviewer does it. The header row's column names are not pinned by a case of their own: cases 1-6 already fail if the four columns stop being failure class, working form, failing form and reason, and pinning the header text as well would make a wording change fail for nothing.

CRITERION 5 (the commands exit 0) is the check list itself, below.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE. One command, from the repository root:

    bash test-repo.sh

That is the closed list: nothing else is run. The full `./test.sh` is deliberately left off — it adds three npm suites and two node suites over code this increment does not touch, and `test-repo.sh` is the only suite whose subject changes here.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED. I ran nothing, not even a baseline: no run would have told me anything I could not read. Expect this: after the test-author's step and before the implementer's, `bash test-repo.sh` exits 1 with exactly the twelve new cases failing (the page does not exist yet) and every pre-existing case passing. After the implementer's step it exits 0.
return.summary: The four-row form table and the ban on exemption clauses get one home, a new path-scoped rule page .claude/rules/authoring.md that loads for whoever opens a file under skills/ or agents/, with a one-sentence pointer from each of the two existing authoring pages and twelve new cases in test-repo.sh. The shared brief was rejected as the home because it ships to every project and binds agents at run time, not the people who write uroboros pages.
